newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian leaders to discuss Ieng Sary with King.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian leaders to discuss Ieng Sary with King.

text.p: Cambodia's co-Premiers arrived at the royal palace on Saturday to discuss a pardon for breakaway Khmer Rouge leader Ieng Sary amid conflicting reports on fighting between rival Khmer Rouge factions.

Co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen were to discuss their request that King Norodom Sihanouk pardon Ieng Sary for his role in the genocide of Pol Pot's 1975-79 Khmer Rouge "killing fields" regime, aides to the co-premiers said.

Ieng Sary, who broke with the Khmer Rouge mainstream last month and began peace talks with the government, and Pol Pot were sentenced to death in absentia for their part in the deaths of more than one million people.
Ieng Sary told reporters in his Phnom Malai base last Monday that he could not be blamed for the killings but also asked the government to clarify his legal status if peace talks were to continue.
A member of Ranariddh's cabinet expected Sihanouk to ask parliament to debate the issue before he would decide on granting a pardon.

Sihanouk had said last month that he would only consider granting Ieng Sary an amnesty after receiving written requests from the government and a two-thirds majority of the 120-member national assembly.
Khmer Rouge forces loyal to Pol Pot said on Saturday they had taken control of Pailin, one of two major bases held by Ieng Sary's supporters in the northwest.

But breakaway Khmer Rouge sources contacted by telephone in the border stronghold denied the claim and the government's armed forces deputy chief of staff, Pol Saroeun, told Reuters: "It is not true. Do not believe it."

Radio controlled by the mainstream Khmer Rouge faction, in a broadcast monitored in Phnom Penh, said fighters loyal to Pol Pot controlled Pailin after fighting a small group of dissidents led by Ieng Sary ally Ei Chien near the border.
The radio claimed that Ei Chien had fled from Pailin, a gem-mining and logging centre close to the Thailand border, on September 3.
But Sok Lee, a Khmer Rouge official in Pailin loyal to Ei Chien, also denied the claims, telling Reuters by telephone, "If it is true (that hardliners had taken Pailin), how can I stay here?"
Divisional commanders Ei Chien and Sok Peap said last month they had split with the mainstream Khmer Rouge group and backed Ieng Sary and his moves towards peace and reconciliation.
The Khmer Rouge signed a United Nations brokered peace accord in 1991 but later reneged on the pact and have been fighting the coalition government that emerged from general elections in 1991.
